name: Mebsuta
description: A supergiant of type G8 I 259 parsecs away, 130 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 48329: radius 130.22 +6.01/-5.51 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 4.677 +/- 0.013 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 48329: mass 5.29 +/- 0.04 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 48329: effective temperature 5009 +/- 63 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 48329: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 3.86 +/- 0.17 mas, inverted

text.card: A supergiant of type G8 I, 259 parsecs away: 130 times the Sun's width and 9,636 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 4.677 milliarcseconds, which gives 130.22 solar radii and 5,009 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 48329: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3384529341302871296 (quality A), from 2008A&A...480...91S; Gaia DR3 measures none
